source.title: Truth or Backpropaganda? An Empirical Investigation of Deep Learning Theory
source.authors: Micah Goldblum; Jonas Geiping; Avi Schwarzschild; Michael Moeller; T. Goldstein

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests how explicit parameter-norm regularization affects held-out accuracy and finds that biasing parameters toward larger norms can outperform weight decay, challenging the version that small-norm solutions generalize better. It also reports other findings on optimization and kernel behavior, but those do not test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The reported generalization-relevant results are the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 held-out accuracy comparisons among no weight decay, weight decay, and norm-bias. NTK stability, loss-minimum, and rank results concern constructs not measured in the listed versions. Values cited from earlier work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: Table 3 supplies a direct V3 comparison: convolutional classifiers and a fully connected MLP trained from scratch on normalized CIFAR-10 with SGD and momentum. Most CNNs substantially outperform the MLP; unregularized Fixup ResNet fails to train. The paper's principal norm-regularization claim is outside the supplied versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the norm-regularization conclusion: nonzero norm targets can outperform weight decay, so smaller parameter norms need not be optimal. The full paper also concludes that realistic networks contain suboptimal local minima, WideResNet NTKs depart from predicted width trends, and low rank does not consistently imply robustness.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains models under a norm-bias regularizer, weight decay, and no weight decay, rather than testing the original claim versions' interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Held-out accuracy varies by architecture, dataset normalization, and regularizer. Norm-bias exceeds weight decay for most reported settings, ties it for MobileNetV2 on normalized CIFAR-10, and both regularizers substantially improve ResNet-20 Fixup over no weight decay.

fits_no_version.finding: Norm-bias usually improves test accuracy over weight decay, with a tie for normalized-CIFAR-10 MobileNetV2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Biasing parameter norms toward nonzero targets can improve image-classification accuracy over weight decay.

fits_no_version.finding: NTK stability improves with width for some simple architectures but deteriorates for WideResNets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width-dependent NTK stability depends on architecture and the interaction between batch normalization and skip connections.

fits_no_version.finding: Constructed suboptimal minima have higher maximum Hessian eigenvalues than the default-trained minimum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Certain poorly optimizing initializations yield sharper suboptimal training minima.

fits_no_version.finding: Rank manipulation often leaves clean accuracy similar and does not establish a consistent low-rank robustness advantage.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low effective rank is not necessary for strong clean or adversarial accuracy in the tested networks.

record.problems: No direct test of the supplied claim versions. Accuracy table entries are averages over 10 runs with standard errors, but the main regularizer experiment description says µ is chosen heuristically. Generalization gap values are not reported; results are test accuracies.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the paired natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
Test error beyond the width needed for zero training error. Width-dependent NTK measurements do not establish this; Figure 5 lacks a readable interpolation-threshold comparison in the supplied text.
The causal contribution of local connectivity, learned sparse local connections, convolutional initialization of fully connected networks, and datasets other than CIFAR-10.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning or switching optimizers.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout interventions, small-data regimes, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay. Weight-decay-only comparisons do not test these interventions.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its ranking of generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Memorization-based example removal, random-removal controls, and retraining accuracy.

missing.what: Additional V3 evidence: naturally trained CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 and skipless ResNet-18 attain 94.66% and 92.95% clean accuracy; the naturally trained MLP attains 58.79%. Record architecture-specific training schedules because these are not matched-recipe comparisons.
missing.locator: Table 4; Appendix A.7, Table 9 and training protocols

record.verdict_notes: All extracted accuracy values and standard errors match the supplied tables. The record overlooks the cross-architecture evidence in Table 3. Those comparisons support an architectural performance difference but do not isolate local connectivity as its cause. No supplied claim version asserts that smaller parameter norms necessarily generalize better.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Test-error behavior as width passes the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier generalization.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out comparisons and tuning conditions.
Large-batch versus small-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects, training-set-size regimes, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to training-test gaps.
Removal and retraining of memorized examples and resulting test-accuracy changes.
